detail.abstract: Standard economics textbooks treat supply-demand equilibrium and prices as primitives. This paper argues that the true foundation is fair division: the iterative process by which agents with equal initial entitlements reveal preferences over heterogeneous goods through risk bidding. We generalize Divide-and-Choose to n agents via an iterative proposal-selection mechanism. Greed is punished by discard/delay; roles are symmetric via randomization. The mechanism achieves subjective fairness (deterrence of greed/manipulation) and objective fairness (ex ante role equality). It endogenously generates price discovery, comparative advantage, and efficiency. Preferences are quantified through interaction; prices emerge as shadows of contestation costs. The framework naturally extends to multi-market settings, explaining the emergence of money, merchants, and two distinct modes of value discovery, finding value in discarded "voids" and differentiating value within recognized goods. Together these constitute the engine of economic evolution.

title: Stationary Online Contention Resolution Schemes
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business,  and University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: Stationary Online Contention Resolution Schemes
detail.abstract:
Online contention resolution schemes (OCRSs) are a central tool in Bayesian online selection and resource allocation: they convert fractional ex-ante relaxations into feasible online policies while preserving each marginal probability up to a constant factor. Despite their importance, designing optimal or near-optimal OCRSs is often technically challenging, and many existing constructions/analyses rely on indirect reductions to prophet inequalities and LP duality, resulting in algorithms that are difficult to interpret or implement. 

In this paper, we introduce stationary online contention resolution schemes (S-OCRSs), a permutation-invariant class of OCRSs in which the distribution of the selected feasible set does not depend on the arrival order. We show that S-OCRSs admit an exact distributional characterization together with a universal online implementation. We then develop a general maximum-entropy approach for constructing and analyzing S-OCRSs, reducing the design of online policies to constructing suitable distributions over feasible sets. This yields a conceptually new technical framework for designing simple and possibly improved OCRSs. 

We demonstrate the power of this framework across several canonical feasibility environments. In particular, we obtain an improved (3-\sqrt{5})/2-selectable OCRS for bipartite matchings, attaining the independence benchmark conjectured to be optimal and yielding the best known prophet inequality for this setting. We also obtain a (1-\sqrt{2/(\pi k)} + O(1/k))-selectable OCRS for k-uniform matroids and a simple, explicit 1/2-selectable OCRS for weakly Rayleigh matroids (including all C-representable matroids such as graphic and laminar matroids). These guarantees match the best known bounds, and our framework yields concrete and systematic constructions, providing transparent algorithms in settings where previous OCRSs were implicit or technically involved. We leave the investigation of other feasibility environments to future work.

detail.abstract: This chapter examines the impact of the geopolitical rivalry between the United States and China on the prospects for inclusive innovation in artificial intelligence (AI) development. It argues that escalating techno-nationalist policies—particularly in areas such as export controls, investment restrictions, and supply chain decoupling—pose systemic risks to knowledge sharing and equitable participation in global innovation networks. The authors examine how political and regulatory turbulence undermines collaborative norms, disrupts academic and entrepreneurial ecosystems, and fuels discriminatory practices that marginalize foreign or underrepresented individuals or groups. Drawing on case studies and policy analyses, the chapter highlights how both countries have prioritized national security and technological dominance over inclusion, transparency, and trust. It concludes by urging a recalibration of AI governance strategies to accommodate pluralism and to safeguard inclusive innovation amid intensifying geopolitical tension.

detail.abstract: Information is what the user makes of it and different users will reach different probabilities from the same information. We consider how "naive" users, who overstate the firm's probability of success, inflate the asset price and harm both themselves and market efficiency by pricing "sophisticated" investors out of the market. Surprising results reveal how all investors benefit by "underbetting their beliefs" or betting as if they are more risk averse than they are. Drawing on models of underbetting developed by mathematicians, we explain how investors who accept that their probabilities are error prone react by investing conservatively, as if they discount indications that seem to warrant a larger "bet". While not raised in accounting theory, traditional accounting conservatism can induce underbetting with the same benefits that gamblers find, in fact generally more so because the share price is lower in a more prudent or risk averse market.

detail.abstract: This report provides an exhaustive analysis of the Just Transition, trac- ing its evolution from a niche labor-oriented concept to a holistic global develop- ment paradigm. By rigorously examining the theoretical underpinnings provided by academia and international organizations—including the ILO, World Bank, ADB, and UNDP—we establish a baseline for understanding the diverse interpretations of justice in the climate context. Furthermore, this analysis interrogates the essential link between Just Transition strategies and the realization of Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) under the Paris Agreement. A central focus of this report is the complex trade-off emerging economies face in balancing economic growth with climate mitigation. Through a detailed comparative analysis of six key nations— Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand, India, Brazil, and South Africa—we identify the systemic policy gaps, financing barriers, and governance failures that currently hinder successful implementation.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a structural account of luxury that shifts attention from objects and brands to the way systems allocate surplus time, energy and security once basic responsibilities have been met. Drawing on sociology, biology, evolutionary game theory and responsibility ethics, I distinguish three analytically separate phenomena that are normally conflated under the word "luxury": luxury as a life-structure of accessible structural leisure; luxury goods as status necessities in specific games; and pseudo-luxury as mimetic overdrafts paid for with future harm. The argument is formalised through an energetic model with survival needs, buffers and surplus, and through a responsibility ledger that tracks how non-deferrable obligations, resilience and discretionary surplus interact. I introduce luxury and pseudo-luxury coefficients that describe how much surplus is devoted to reversible leisure, to deepening redundancy, or to fragile signals that erode health and buffers. Case studies from literature and contemporary consumption illustrate how different groups position themselves within this space. Rather than moralising consumption, the framework explains who can afford what kinds of surplus, how signals are financed, and why time and attention emerge as the primary modern luxury on which all others depend.

detail.abstract:
Despite sustained global liquidity and persistent interest in African infrastructure, energy, and industrial projects, cross-border investment across the continent remains constrained. Dominant explanations emphasize capital scarcity, project quality, or macroeconomic instability. This paper advances a different argument: that many investment failures are rooted in deficiencies of institutional trust and execution, particularly at the level of deal origination, professional coordination, and accountability across jurisdictions.

The paper examines the African Global Investment Corridor (AGIC) as an exploratory design case of a governed deal origination and execution system embedded within a constitutional professional network. AGIC is not a financial intermediary or investment fund. Rather, it is an institutional architecture that governs how investment opportunities are originated, structured, executed, and monitored by decentralized legal and advisory actors who already operate within African markets.

Central to the model is the recognition that deal origination is multi-vector: investment opportunities emerge through multiple channels, including professional networks, investor-initiated mandates, and policy-generated pipelines. AGIC provides a unified governance spine through which these heterogeneous entry pathways converge into a single, rule-bound execution process. 

The architecture further incorporates corridor-based institutional differentiation, through which engagement frameworks are adapted to distinct regional investment environments while preserving centralized execution standards and accountability. By integrating socio-technical governance mechanisms with procedural authority over execution, the paper contributes a reference design for engineering institutional trust in high-risk, multi-jurisdictional investment environments.

title: Fair Auction

detail.title: Fair Auction
detail.abstract: Traditional auction mechanisms, despite their theoretical elegance, often fail in practice due to perceived unfairness, weak incentives for information acquisition, and insufficient compensation for the second-highest bidder, who serves as the critical price anchor. This paper identifies these shortcomings,particularly in winner-takes-all design and proposes a novel sealed-bid mechanism called the Fair Auction. By transforming the highest and second-highest bidders into interchangeable roles of Buyer and Anchor, with rewards and penalties allocated based on the bid difference, the Fair Auction provides real incentives for aggressive bidding, protects bidder information, and increases expected seller revenue while promoting perceived fairness.

title: China Economy Enters the Post-Stimulus Era

detail.title: China Economy Enters the Post-Stimulus Era
detail.abstract: China's economy, the world's second-largest, is at a crossroads. Post-pandemic recovery has been less robust than expected, leading to mounting internal and external challenges. A shift in China's economic model seems inevitable, moving from a heavy reliance on economic stimulus to more sustainable, consumer-driven growth. This shift, however, raises fundamental questions about the efficacy of policy strategies employed over the past few decades.

title: A Two-Dimensional Risk Framework for AI in Mental Health Software as a Medical Device

detail.title: A Two-Dimensional Risk Framework for AI in Mental Health Software as a Medical Device

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is founder and CEO of DivergentFlow, PBC, a Public Benefits Corporation developing AI-enabled mental health tools. DivergentFlow is a stakeholder in the industry this framework would regulate.
declarations.funderStatement: This work received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
This paper proposes a Two-Dimensional Risk Framework for regulating AI-enabled mental health Software as a Medical Device (SaMD), submitted to the FDA Digital Health Advisory Committee (Docket FDA-2025-N-2338). The framework moves regulation beyond static technology classification to dynamic, context-specific patient risk by evaluating devices along two dimensions: Severity of Harm (using existing IMDRF categories I-IV) and Total Failure Probability, which accounts for Technical, Human, and Contextual failure modes. Risk is defined as Severity × Failure Probability. This approach reveals why identical technology — such as a depression screener — requires different regulatory oversight when used by a clinician in a controlled setting versus a consumer self-diagnosing at home.

The paper argues that the primary mechanism for reducing failure probability is Architectural Safety through the Principle of Least Capability: using the simplest sufficient technology for each system function. By decomposing AI systems into modular, bounded components that structurally lack the capability to produce dangerous or unbounded outputs, developers can ensure that failure is predictable, safe, and isolated. For high-risk devices (IMDRF III-IV), this principle necessitates specific controls including Model Version Locking with cryptographic checksums, Deterministic Operation (temperature=0.0), and prohibition of external API dependencies for core logic — mirroring pharmaceutical supply chain standards.

The framework further addresses bias through lifecycle management, requiring that worst-case demographic subgroup performance remain within 80% of the overall average, and extends the FDA's Predetermined Change Control Plan (PCCP) mechanism to cover AI-specific failure modes. An Innovation Ladder provides a phased growth path for startups, aligning regulatory stringency with clinical evidence and available capital at each tier.

The paper concludes that safety-first design is not a regulatory burden but an economic imperative: it lowers operational costs, minimizes liability, and builds the trust necessary for sustainable adoption. Clear regulatory requirements enable rather than stifle innovation.

title: Petropolitics 101: The Case of Guyana

detail.title: Petropolitics 101: The Case of Guyana
detail.abstract: Nearly five years after discovering massive offshore oil reserves, the South American nation of Guyana confronted a disputed election in 2020 that exposed the volatile intersection of petroleum wealth and ethno-political division. This paper examines Guyana's emerging oil economy through the lens of petropolitics and resource curse theory, analyzing how the country's unique ethnic composition, divided principally between Afro-Guyanese and Indo-Guyanese communities descended from slaves and indentured servants, shapes the political contest over newfound hydrocarbon revenues. The analysis traces Guyana's political history as a microcosm of Cold War geopolitics, including US and British interference that sustained the People's National Congress in power for 27 years, through decades of chronic mismanagement necessitating IMF structural adjustment, to the present contest between the PNC and People's Progressive Party. The paper critically assesses the terms of Guyana's negotiations with ExxonMobil, which critics argue disproportionately favor the multinational, and evaluates the structural impediments to broad-based development, including an underdeveloped workforce, high emigration rates, and heavy reliance on imported expertise. The analysis examines the government's establishment of a Sovereign Wealth Fund for petroleum revenues, identifying concerns over the absence of detailed investment guidance and the country's poor track record on transparency and regulatory implementation. The paper further considers Guyana's diversification prospects, particularly in services and tourism, and the urgency of a post-oil pivot given the instability of crude prices amid the Saudi-Russian price war. The paper concludes that in the absence of electoral transparency, public confidence in institutions, and robust regulatory oversight, Guyana risks replicating the resource curse pathologies of its neighbors rather than realizing the transformative development its leaders envision.

title: Reevaluating ERISA Fiduciary Relationships as Relational Contracts
affiliations: Texas Tech University School of Law

detail.title: Reevaluating ERISA Fiduciary Relationships as Relational Contracts
detail.abstract:
Excessive fiduciary fees exacted from retirement savings exacerbate an overlooked crisis in which Americans descend into poverty after decades of work. Though ERISA fiduciary relationships and their associated fees are memorialized through contracts, most analysis by courts and scholars centers on ERISA's foundation in trust law. Examining ERISA fiduciary arrangements as relational contracts exposes structural misalignments in fee compositions, incentive mechanisms, and core fiduciary duties. It also supplies tools for redesigning these relationships to better protect American workers-without the need for congressional or regulatory intervention. 

Drawing from the robust cross-disciplinary literature on relational contracts, this Article explores how relational contract principles should inform analyses-and restructuring-of the contracts underpinning the ERISA fiduciary arrangement. It contributes by proposing practicable revisions to fiduciary arrangements that rectify suboptimal fiduciary compensation structures and lopsided risk allocation. With the aim of preserving the $13 trillion in assets defined contribution retirement plans hold, this Article proposes incentivization and bonding mechanisms previously unapplied in the ERISA fiduciary context.

title: CST Series 12: Entropy Coordinates in Conserved Settlement Theory
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: CST Series 12: Entropy Coordinates in Conserved Settlement Theory
detail.abstract: Conserved Settlement Theory (CST) models the international monetary system as a settlement process governed by the interaction between elastic financial claims and a conserved settlement base. Settlement slack summarizes the balance between these quantities. This paper derives an entropy coordinate representation of settlement slack. The transformation converts multiplicative slack dynamics into an additive state variable centered at the settlement boundary. The resulting formulation provides a compact representation of settlement pressure, equilibrium drift, oscillatory adjustment, and volatility regimes. The entropy formulation clarifies the regime structure of CST. When settlement slack approaches unity the settlement constraint binds and price becomes the marginal mechanism of adjustment. In this regime the system fluctuates around the constraint and price responses become increasingly convex when settlement pressure emerges.

title: A Different Contagion: India's Bank Bailouts

detail.title: A Different Contagion: India's Bank Bailouts
detail.abstract: The Indian government's 2020 bailout of YES Bank, the country's fifth-largest private bank, signaled the deepening of a systemic banking crisis coinciding with the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic. This paper examines the structural vulnerabilities of India's financial sector, arguing that the crisis is the predictable result of overextended lending, weak corporate governance, and inadequate regulatory oversight that long predates the Modi administration. The analysis traces how the exuberance surrounding market-friendly reforms precipitated a surge in credit markets for which India's expansive and unstable banking sector was ill-prepared, producing dangerous levels of speculation and rising non-performing loans across both parastatal and private institutions. The paper pays particular attention to the role of non-bank financial companies, or shadow banks, whose ability to circumvent traditional regulatory regimes cultivated a culture of high-risk lending, with the 2018 collapse of Infrastructure Leasing and Financial Services serving as the first major manifestation of systemic distress. The analysis critically evaluates the government's response, including its preference for public-private partnerships over taxpayer-funded rescues and cosmetic reforms such as executive replacements that fail to address underlying structural ailments. The paper identifies a compounding risk in the bailout strategy itself, as healthier lenders are compelled to take equity stakes in failing institutions, spreading exposure to weak assets across a shrinking pool of solvent banks. The paper further examines proposals for deeper reform, including expanding the Reserve Bank of India's supervisory capacity, enforcing accountability mechanisms, and imposing meaningful penalties on negligent executives. The paper concludes that India's banking contagion, though overshadowed by the pandemic, poses ramifications that could persist far longer, and that absent structural reform, the government's reactive bailout approach is unlikely to produce more than a continuation of the status quo.

title: Sectoral Vulnerability to Climate Change: Distributional Evidence from Spatially Heterogeneous Economies
affiliations: Hankuk University of Foreign Studies and

detail.title: Sectoral Vulnerability to Climate Change: Distributional Evidence from Spatially Heterogeneous Economies
detail.abstract: We develop a distributional regression framework to quantify heterogeneous sectoral impacts of climate change by linking spatial temperature shocks to cross-sectional growth outcomes. Starting from a climate-augmented regional growth model, we show that aggregating heterogeneous regional responses into scalar averages obscures economically relevant distributional mechanisms, motivating an approach that treats temperature anomalies and sectoral growth as distribution-valued objects. Using global data on land temperature anomalies and subnational sectoral output, we estimate sector-specific distributional response functions that map climate perturbations into reallocations of probability mass across the growth distribution. We find that temperature shocks systematically shift mass toward adverse growth realizations, with effects concentrated in the lower tail and strongest in agriculture, intermediate in manufacturing, and attenuated in services. Decomposing shocks further shows that sustained global warming induces broad-based distributional degradation, whereas episodic El Niño events primarily amplify downside tail risk, highlighting the limitations of mean-based damage assessments.

title: Strategic Determination of Settlement Tolerance in Conserved Settlement Theory
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Strategic Determination of Settlement Tolerance in Conserved Settlement Theory
detail.abstract: Conserved Settlement Theory (CST) represents the international monetary system as a settlement constraint linking elastic claims to a conserved settlement base. Earlier papers in the series define settlement slack as the central state variable, derive the local price equation of the conserved settlement asset, and prove asymptotic convergence of the system toward the conserved settlement boundary. This note develops the strategic layer underlying the institutional leverage parameter k. The key claim is that k is not merely an exogenous coefficient but a strategic equilibrium variable reflecting the willingness of states and institutions to tolerate liability-based settlement. Policies such as reserve diversification, sanctions, managed exchange rates, and alternative clearing arrangements therefore operate primarily through k, while the price of the conserved settlement asset adjusts mechanically as its inverse shadow expression.

title: Shadow Price Dynamics of the Conserved Settlement Boundary
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Shadow Price Dynamics of the Conserved Settlement Boundary
detail.abstract: Conserved Settlement Theory (CST) models the international monetary system as a constraint system in which elastic financial claims must ultimately be settled using a conserved asset. This paper derives the local price dynamics of the conserved settlement asset directly from the settlement state variable. Because the state variable depends monotonically on price, feasibility restoration determines the direction of price adjustment. The resulting local dynamics take the form Ṗ = β(1-ϕ) with β > 0. Together with previously established Lyapunov stability results, this completes the dynamic characterization of the conserved settlement boundary.

title: Conserved Settlement Theory (CST): Reference Dictionary
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Conserved Settlement Theory (CST): Reference Dictionary
detail.abstract: Conserved Settlement Theory (CST) models the international monetary system as elastic financial claims E expanding against a conserved settlement asset Q. Because claims can grow faster than settlement capacity, price adjusts dynamically to keep the system near a settlement constraint. The equilibrium settlement price is P ∗ = E/(kQ). Observed price can be written P = P ∗es, where s = ln ϕ measures deviations from equilibrium and typically oscillates around 0 while P ∗(t) can drift over time.

title: Guns Are Lethal: The History of Five Centuries of Continuing Improvements in Firearms Efficacy
affiliations: Independence Institute

detail.title: Guns Are Lethal: The History of Five Centuries of Continuing Improvements in Firearms Efficacy
detail.abstract:
This Article critiques emerging civil lawsuits that aim to hold firearms manufacturers liable for failing to reduce the "lethality" of civilian-market guns. Such suits are fundamentally flawed because firearms were invented five centuries ago explicitly to harm human adversaries, and every major technological advancement since then has improved their efficacy for that core purpose-whether measured in kinetic energy, accuracy, reliability, reloading speed, or practical availability. 

Part I examines factors that enhance firearms lethality, including kinetic energy, accuracy (influenced by barrel length, ergonomics, sights, and recoil management), reliability, reloading speed, affordability, and portability. It notes that practical lethality often depends on context: very high-power rifles like the .50 BMG Barrett are rarely used in crime due to size and cost, while compact, affordable handguns dominate homicide statistics despite lower raw power, because they are more readily available for both criminal and defensive use.

Part II demonstrates that American constitutional protections for the right to arms—federal and state—overwhelmingly emphasize lethal purposes: militia/collective defense, personal and family self-defense (requiring “fight-stopping hits”), and hunting (demanding quick, humane kills). These purposes are incompatible with mandates to diminish lethality.

Part III introduces military historian Trevor N. Dupuy’s Theoretical Lethality Index (TLI), a quantitative metric designed for militia/combat contexts, based on rate of fire, reliability, range, accuracy, and relative effectiveness. The TLI shows dramatic increases over time:  from 10 for the 16th-century arquebus, to 495 for the 1903 Springfield rifle, and 640 for a modern AR-15 platform.

Part IV traces American firearms evolution from colonial matchlocks and flintlocks through 19th-century breakthroughs (percussion ignition, interchangeable parts, conoidal bullets, metallic cartridges, breechloading, mechanisms, smokeless powder, semiautomatics) to 20th- and 21st-century refinements (improved materials, optics). The most revolutionary leaps occurred in the 19th century; modern consumer firearms represent merely incremental improvements on designs from a century ago.

The Article concludes that because virtually every enhancement serving legitimate defensive, hunting, or militia uses also increases potential for misuse, efforts to impose tort liability for “excessive” lethality conflict with centuries of constitutional recognition of firearms' inherently lethal role in the constitutional right to arms.

title: Policy Blind Spots
affiliations: University of Wyoming

detail.title: Policy Blind Spots

declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was provided by the IRB of my institution.

detail.abstract: Despite their desirable properties, carbon taxes have received low public support. Leading explanations attribute the rejection of carbon taxes to preferences and ideology. We show that voters make mistakes when reasoning about the consequences of such policies. We focus on leading versions of carbon taxes that are designed to draw wide public support by issuing dividend payments from collected revenues, resulting in a policy that is progressive and produces more winners than losers. Using experiments, we show that subjects have specific blind spots in reasoning about policies with taxes and dividends, even when described simply and in incentivized, abstract settings that remove scope for preferences and ideologies. Based on these findings, we introduce a new policy that is isomorphic to a leading carbon tax proposal, but engineered to be robust to these cognitive frictions. In a U.S. survey conducted in Summer 2023 we find that our new policy (which we call carbon penalty and reward) garners 30 percentage points more public support than the original proposal (known as carbon fee and dividend). Using independent measures, we show that this increase in support is concentrated in people who have difficulty reasoning about the policy structure.

title: Routing the Dollar: Gateway Infrastructure, Monetary Policy Transmission, and the Dollar's International Functions in Digital Markets

detail.title: Routing the Dollar: Gateway Infrastructure, Monetary Policy Transmission, and the Dollar's International Functions in Digital Markets

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: Self

detail.abstract:
Dollar stablecoins extend the dollar’s exchange, store-of-value, and funding functions into blockchain markets, largely outside the Federal Reserve’s standard supervisory and reporting perimeter, though not necessarily outside all federal or state oversight. We argue the policy-relevant unit of analysis is not the token but the gateway (the issuer, exchange, or protocol that routes stablecoin value) because the same dollar token inherits different compliance, monetary, and safe-haven properties depending on which gateway processes it.

Using daily Ethereum gateway transfer volumes (19 entities, 51 addresses, 27.7 percent of USDC/USDT value), monthly counterparty networks (15 gateways, 35 months, 3,804 unique dyads), and stress-episode windows around the Silicon Valley Bank (SVB) crisis and the Binance USD (BUSD) regulatory action, we report three descriptive findings.

First, stablecoin supply is cointegrated with Fed balance-sheet variables in a regime-dependent way; a Treasury bill minus on-chain lending-rate spread provides mechanism-consistent opportunity-cost evidence. The relationship is dollar-specific, absent for Bitcoin or Ethereum. Cointegration is strongest during quantitative tightening (trace = 48.18) and weakens during easing (trace = 17.71) even as level correlations remain strong (r = −0.98).

Second, that co-movement distributes unevenly across the gateway layer: institutional gateways (both regulated and offshore) share the aggregate inverse relationship with Fed assets while permissionless protocols trend in the opposite direction, and the routing network is concentrating; volume doubled over three years while unique counterparties declined 25 percent and cross-gateway counterparties fell from 5.8 to 2.6 percent.

Third, within the dollar-pegged settlement instruments we observe, stress behavior is gateway-contingent: capital routes across gateways rather than out of dollar-pegged stablecoins, with tier share recovery coinciding with the SVB intervention sequence and the restoration of USDC convertibility, though causal attribution across intervention tools is not identified. Fragmentation manifests primarily as competition and concentration within the dollar’s own gateway infrastructure, rather than as substitution into non-dollar-pegged instruments. For monitoring purposes, gateway-level flow data are more informative than token-level aggregates for assessing regulatory exposure, concentration risk, and stress routing.

title: Local Aspects of Digital Competition: Evidence from a Meal Delivery Platform in Germany
affiliations: University of Düsseldorf - Düsseldorf Institute for Competition Economics (DICE), The Rockwool Foundation Research Unit, Institute of German Economics (IW) and Institute of German Economics (IW)

detail.title: Local Aspects of Digital Competition: Evidence from a Meal Delivery Platform in Germany

keywords: Local Socioeconomic Factors JEL classification: D40

detail.abstract: We study competition in the ready-to-eat meal delivery market in Germany, a sector characterized by digital platforms, while the competition is tightly local. We investigate how competition intensity varies spatially and with socioeconomic factors and how competition intensity maps into prices. To address these questions, we combine standardized product, price, and vendor-level data scraped from Just Eat Germany (lieferando.de) with socioeconomic characteristics on the postal code level. We find that higher competition intensity in the relevant delivery market is associated with lower meal prices but higher beverage prices, suggesting differentiated pricing strategies across product categories. Regions characterized by stronger overall competition experience greater price pressure. Despite substantially higher purchasing power in West Germany, average price levels are comparable between East and West. This seems to result from more pronounced competition-induced price reductions in West Germany.

title: Predictive Power of Inflation Expectations in India
affiliations: Government of India - Reserve Bank of India and Government of India - Reserve Bank of India

detail.title: Predictive Power of Inflation Expectations in India

publicationDetails.detailsText: Singh and Gupta (2026). Predictive Power of Inflation Expectations in India. Economic and Political Weekly, Special Article, Vol. 61, Issue No. 4, 42-50.

detail.abstract: Inflation expectations influence how societies spend, save, and govern, shaping both economic behaviour and policy effectiveness. This study compares household and business inflation expectations in India and their predictive power for actual inflation. Business inflation expectations became more volatile post pandemic, reflecting macroeconomic uncertainty, while household expectations remained stable under the post-flexible inflation targeting regime. Empirical results show that households’ expectations better explain consumer price index inflation, whereas business expectations align more with wholesale price index trends. The increasing relevance of households’ expectations for core CPI suggests a strengthening of the inflation expectations channel in recent years.

title: Structural Obsolescence of Keynesian Monetary Policy: Bitcoin's Protocol as the Mechanism That Renders Interventionist Demand Management Inoperable The Realignment Trilogy – Capstone
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Structural Obsolescence of Keynesian Monetary Policy: Bitcoin's Protocol as the Mechanism That Renders Interventionist Demand Management Inoperable The Realignment Trilogy – Capstone
detail.abstract: This paper is the third and culminating installment in The Realignment Trilogy, integrating the Fiat Stratification Feedback Model (Quinby 2026a) and the Bitcoin Dismantlement Framework (Quinby 2026b). It demonstrates that Bitcoin's protocol properties, including its fixed supply of 21 million units, decentralized issuance through proof-of-work, and bearer-asset design, render the transmission mechanisms of Keynesian demand management structurally inoperable. The analysis forges a direct before-and-after linkage between the self-reinforcing loops of fractional-reserve lending, Cantillon effects, K-shaped divergence, and buy-borrow-die incentives under fiat conditions and their systematic neutralization under Bitcoin. This linkage constitutes the novel scholarly contribution of the trilogy: the two antecedent papers together provide the first closed-loop model explaining why Keynesian interventionist frameworks, fully operational within pure fiat monetary architectures, lose structural efficacy as Bitcoin adoption reaches sufficient thresholds. The paper maintains a parallel structure with the antecedent works for direct comparability. It grounds the discussion in Austrian economic principles of sound money and monetary non-neutrality while contrasting these with Keynesian assumptions regarding liquidity preference, multiplier effects, discretionary stimulus, aggregate demand management, and Phillips-curve trade-offs. Empirical anchors from on-chain data and Federal Reserve reports support the mechanisms, alongside a neutral historical context and explicit acknowledgment of transitional challenges and data limitations. This work positions itself as a neutral, mechanism-focused contribution to monetary theory.

title: Copyright, Freedom of Speech and the Insult to the National Anthem

detail.title: Copyright, Freedom of Speech and the Insult to the National Anthem
detail.abstract: After a great deal of back-and-forth debate, the National Anthem Ordinance was finally passed in Hong Kong on 12 June 2020. The newly introduced offences criminalise certain forms of insulting behaviour towards the national anthem. This article aims to discuss the intricate relationship among the protection of the national anthem from copyright infringement, the freedom of expression of the public and the newly introduced offences. Any alteration to the national anthem can not only potentially infringe the economic and moral rights of the author but also constitute criminal offences of insulting behaviour related to the national anthem. This article also finds that critical alterations of the national anthem as expressions (e.g. parodies or satires) are not well protected under the copyright laws in both mainland China and Hong Kong. The higher risk lies in the abridgement of the freedom of expression brought out by the newly introduced criminal offences and also latest technological advancements. This article also suggests that the copyright laws in both mainland China and Hong Kong must explicitly recognise parody and satire as acceptable exceptions to the economic and moral rights enjoyed by both the author and the copyright owner and thereby empower the courts to better delimit the boundaries between tolerable expressions and insulting behaviours over the national anthem when faced with constitutional challenges. "And ever again the human race will from time to time decree: 'There is something one is absolutely forbidden henceforth to laugh at.' " 1-Friedrich Nietzsche

title: Regional Housing Vacancy Cycle Interdependencies and Asymmetries: A Markov-Switching Analysis
affiliations: University of Connecticut - School of Business, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis - Research Division, Heartland Forward and University of North Carolina  (UNC) at Wilmington

detail.title: Regional Housing Vacancy Cycle Interdependencies and Asymmetries: A Markov-Switching Analysis

declarations.ethicsApproval: There are no human subjects in this study.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates the non-linear dynamics and interdependencies of regional homeowner vacancy rates in the United States. Utilizing a Markov-Switching Vector Autoregression (MS-VAR) framework, we identify distinct vacancy rate regimes-characterized as low, intermediate, and high-and examine the synchronization of these cycles across the Northeast, Midwest, South, and West. Unlike traditional linear models that assume a constant natural vacancy rate, our approach explicitly models endogenous regime shifts to capture the asymmetric adjustments of housing markets to shocks. We find that fluctuations in regional vacancy rates are driven significantly by interregional spillovers, particularly regarding population movement into a region. Furthermore, we document substantial heterogeneity in how these shocks propagate depending on the prevailing vacancy regime. These state-dependent dynamics suggest that the effectiveness of demand-or supply-side housing policies is likely conditional on the vacancy regime in a region.

title: Spurious Fit in Thin Markets: A Preprocessing Cautionary Tale Using Puerto Rico GO Spreads

detail.title: Spurious Fit in Thin Markets: A Preprocessing Cautionary Tale Using Puerto Rico GO Spreads
detail.abstract: Post-restructuring Puerto Rico GO bond spreads achieve strong in-sample fit but fail dramatically in walk-forward evaluation. Using transaction-level yields from EMMA for the most actively traded Series 2022A maturities, matched to constant-maturity U.S. Treasury yields from FRED, I construct a monthly fiscal-stress signal from maturity matched spreads in a thin municipal market. In a burn-in window, a one-lag predictive regression of Puerto Rico economic activity on the lagged spread signal produces a high in-sample R 2 (about 0.52) and a permutation-style p-value of 0.006. However, pseudo out-of-sample performance collapses: out-of-sample R 2 values are deeply negative (about-6.4 to-8.3), and an AR(1) benchmark dominates. A forensic preprocessing audit shows that carry-forward rules and EWMA smoothing do not materially affect conclusions, while the rolling standardization window is decisive. Short (126-day) rolling Z-scores induce an adaptive regressor that fits local regimes in the training period but does not generalize; extending the window to 252 days sharply improves walk-forward performance yet eliminates in-sample significance, indicating no stable predictive content. The results highlight that in thin markets, preprocessing choices can manufacture apparent predictability and walk-forward validation is essential.

title: Infusing Tax Policymaking With Economic Dignity
affiliations: William S. Richardson School of Law, University of Hawaii

detail.title: Infusing Tax Policymaking With Economic Dignity

publicationDetails.detailsText: University of Hawai’i Richardson School of Law Research Paper
publicationDetails.journalName: University of Hawai'i William S. Richardson School of Law Legal Studies Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
This article contends the human right to dignity—the inherent, equal, and inalienable worth of every person—is a unique and essential lens to evaluate tax policy and systems. Integral components of economic dignity—people’s capacity to financially provide for their family, pursue purpose and potential, and partake freely in the economy—are impacted by these polices and systems. Economic dignity necessitates that all individuals be provided with access to opportunities. Tax systems must be evaluated to determine the effect of their policies at the human level—an average working citizen—and ensure benefits do not accrue only to those with substantial accumulated wealth or of a certain class, race, or ethnicity. Our current federal and state tax systems do just that systemically.  

“Each individual has a universal responsibility to shape institutions to serve human needs.”

title: Systemic Misalignments in India's Clean Energy Transition: An Analysis of Policy, Financial, Institutional, and Supply Chain Barriers
affiliations: Tyche Investments - Climate Consulting Group

detail.title: Systemic Misalignments in India's Clean Energy Transition: An Analysis of Policy, Financial, Institutional, and Supply Chain Barriers
detail.abstract: India's ambitious target of 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030 positions renewable energy at the center of its development strategy. However, the pace of adoption remains below required trajectories. This study investigates the key policy, financial, institutional, and supply chain barriers to India's clean energy transition and analyzes how misalignments between these systems affect the pace of renewable energy adoption. A systematic literature review of academic sources is conducted, employing a four-system analytical framework. The findings reveal that barriers are deeply interconnected: policy inconsistency at the state level elevates perceived investment risk, raising the cost of capital; institutional delays in land acquisition and clearances intersect with supply chain disruptions to stall project execution; and DISCOM financial weakness undermines offtake, perpetuating a cycle of high risk and expensive finance. The analysis, demonstrates that misalignments between systems compound to slow adoption more than any single category of barrier in isolation. The failure of Renewable Purchase Obligations exemplifies how a single mechanism can be paralyzed by multi-system weaknesses. The study concludes that accelerating India's energy transition requires coordinated, systemic interventions addressing DISCOM reform, institutional capacity building, supply chain diversification, and innovative financial instruments. Piecemeal approaches targeting individual barriers are insufficient; what is needed is a holistic strategy that aligns policy, finance, institutions, and supply chains to unlock the pace required to meet India's climate commitments.

title: Impact Is Not ESG: Evidence of Distinct Constructs and Private-Public Pricing Divide
affiliations: Morningstar Investment Management, LLC.

detail.title: Impact Is Not ESG: Evidence of Distinct Constructs and Private-Public Pricing Divide
detail.abstract: Impact investing and ESG are compared using empirical data and quantitative methods. A sample is constructed from PitchBook private equity data and Morningstar Direct public market data for analysis. The results indicate that impact investing and ESG are distinct constructs. Impact-alignment and ESG capture different attributes of portfolio companies. Portfolio companies spanning the lifecycle from the private market through IPO to the public market are studied. In the private market, impact-aligned portfolio companies underperform relative to their non-impact-aligned counterparts. In the secondary market, impact-aligned and non-impact-aligned portfolio companies exhibit similar valuation dynamics. This finding indicates that impact-alignment does not significantly affect public market performance. In contrast, ESG risk influences both private and public market performance. Portfolio companies with high ESG risk outperform those with low ESG risk in the private market and during the initial post-IPO trading period.

title: Encumbered Settlement in Conserved Settlement Theory
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Encumbered Settlement in Conserved Settlement Theory
detail.abstract: Conserved Settlement Theory (CST) models international monetary adjustment as a constraint feedback system governed by the relationship between settlement slack and the price of conserved settlement capacity. The minimal dynamic model assumes that the conserved settlement base is fully available to perform settlement. In practice, portions of the settlement base may be encumbered through lending, swaps, collateral reuse, or rehypothecation. Encumbrance both reduces the amount of settlement capacity available for final settlement and simultaneously supports additional financial claims. This note introduces a compact representation of encumbered settlement and derives the resulting expression for true settlement slack. The analysis shows that encumbrance compresses settlement slack from both sides of the balance sheet, suppresses observable volatility in slack, and produces nonlinear tightening of the settlement constraint. As the system approaches the settlement boundary, the capacity for encumbrance collapses and settlement must occur directly in the conserved asset. These results integrate naturally with the CST frontier dynamic equations and provide a structural explanation for extended periods of apparent stability followed by rapid repricing of conserved settlement assets.

title: The Sky Is Falling: Immigration Law and Agency Adjudicator Independence
affiliations: Widener University - Commonwealth Law School

detail.title: The Sky Is Falling: Immigration Law and Agency Adjudicator Independence

publicationDetails.detailsText: Widener Law Commonwealth Research Paper No. 25-14
publicationDetails.journalName: Widener University Commonwealth Law School Legal Studies Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This article examines the degradation of agency decisional independence under unitary executive theory through the experience of immigration law. The Supreme Court is expected to overturn 90 years of precedent this term, in Trump v. Slaughter, by embracing unitary executive theory to hold that Congress may not limit the president's power to fire the head of an agency. Congress has protected some agency heads with "for cause" removal restrictions that do not allow the president to fire the agency head for political reasons. Slaughter threatens the category of "independent agency" and could upset fundamental understandings of the structure of government. During the oral argument in Slaughter, Solicitor General Bauer asserted that the "sky will not fall" if the Supreme Court eliminates independent agencies. This article asserts that the experience of immigration law shows the opposite; the sky is falling.

title: Alternate Investment Funds and Retirement Adequacy in India
affiliations: University of Mumbai

detail.title: Alternate Investment Funds and Retirement Adequacy in India
detail.abstract: India's National Pension Scheme restricts alternative investments to five percent of portfolio value. This restriction applies uniformly to Sovereign Gold Bonds, listed REITs, and leveraged private equity funds despite their vastly different risk profiles. This paper examines whether such uniform treatment satisfies constitutional standards of rational classification under Article 14. The analysis suggests the framework creates internal inconsistencies. Sovereign Gold Bonds carry government guarantees and exhibit lower volatility than equities, yet face stricter allocation limits than equity securities. The regulatory justification citing market immaturity and subscriber protection applies unevenly across instruments within the alternative category. This paper proposes a provisional risk-differentiated framework to test the internal coherence of existing regulation. The argument is not that courts should invalidate current rules, but that PFRDA should articulate why instruments with fundamentally different risk characteristics warrant identical regulatory treatment. Without such justification, the framework appears to lack the rational nexus to stated objectives that Article 14 requires.

title: Impacts of Climate Change Effects on Renewable Energy Systems

detail.title: Impacts of Climate Change Effects on Renewable Energy Systems

detail.abstract: Climate change is reshaping the global energy landscape, not only intensifying the urgency for clean and sustainable power but also influencing how renewable energy systems themselves perform. Rising temperatures, shifting weather patterns, increasing frequency of extreme events, and long-term changes in wind, solar radiation, and hydrological cycles are altering the reliability, efficiency, and planning of renewable technologies. As we strive toward a low-carbon future, it becomes critical to understand how these evolving climate dynamics affect energy production, infrastructure resilience, and system optimization. Today’s seminar aims to explore these interconnected challenges and opportunities, providing a scientific foundation for research on ‘renewable energy systems’ that these remain robust and effective in a rapidly changing climate. Importantly, returning to renewables to help mitigate climate change is an excellent approach which needs to be sustainable in order to meet energy demand of future generations. Building on this understanding, it is essential to examine how technological advancements, adaptive system design, and integrated planning can mitigate the risks posed by climate variability while enhancing renewable energy performance. Innovations such as climate-responsive forecasting tools, resilient grid architectures, energy storage solutions, and hybrid renewable configurations offer promising pathways to maintain stability and efficiency under uncertain future conditions.  At the same time, policy frameworks, stakeholder collaboration, and data-driven decision-making play a pivotal role in translating scientific insights into practical, scalable solutions. By exploring these dimensions, we can better prepare renewable energy systems not only to withstand climate change but to thrive in helping society transition toward a more secure and sustainable energy future. In this light, cultivating a deep knowledge of the world of renewable energy becomes indispensable - not only to appreciate the diversity of technologies available, but also to recognize the global energy challenges they are designed to address. Understanding the energy problem and its potential solutions allows us to contextualize the role of renewables within broader socioeconomic and environmental goals. Equally important is grasping the intricate climate–renewable energy nexus, where climate dynamics shape energy potential and, conversely, clean energy deployment contributes to climate mitigation. By engaging with these interconnected themes, we open the door to new opportunities for advancing research, fostering innovation, and enriching educational pathways that will empower the next generation of scientists, engineers, and policymakers to drive the clean energy transition forward.

detail.abstract: This work examines the mediation of artificial intelligence in the detection and analysis of human movement in audiovisual contexts, with particular attention to film and advertising, through an interdisciplinary approach that brings together functional, narrative, and legal perspectives. Movement is addressed as a complex object that cannot be reduced either to its technical dimension or to its expressive value, since its algorithmic translation involves decisions that affect the body, the meaning of the image, and the rights of the individuals involved. From a functional standpoint, the study explores how processes of algorithmic optimization tend to normalize bodily gesture, creating tensions with the adaptive 2 variability inherent to human movement. From an audiovisual perspective, it analyzes how these mediations affect the narrative construction of gesture, showing how automatic detection indirectly conditions aesthetic and expressive decisions. In parallel, the legal analysis situates bodily movement as information worthy of protection, raising questions about its capture, reuse, and circulation as data, as well as the attribution of responsibility in processes mediated by automated systems. The work argues that detecting movement is not equivalent to understanding it, and that artificial intelligence operates as a technical mediator that reconfigures gesture according to criteria embedded in its models. Through an applied scenario, the paper illustrates the concrete tensions that emerge when the body is translated into data and reused for creative purposes. As a conclusion, it proposes an integrated approach that preserves the plurality of interpretations of human movement and situates artificial intelligence as a contextual tool, subordinated to functional readings, narrative decisions, and clear normative frameworks.

title: Return to Nature: Biodiversity Loss and Global Stock Returns

detail.title: Return to Nature: Biodiversity Loss and Global Stock Returns

declarations.declarationOfInterest: We acknowledge financial support from Netspar through a Netspar Theme Grant.

detail.abstract: We examine whether biodiversity risk is priced in global equity markets using two new firm-level biodiversity risk measures: an environmental cost-based measure grounded in the IPBES drivers of biodiversity loss and a geospatial measure that links firms' asset locations to key biodiversity areas. Our study encompasses a larger sample than prior research: 12,288 firms across 58 countries over 2009-2022. We find that biodiversity risk matters, but pricing depends on the level of variation in biodiversity risk. Within firms, higher biodiversity risk is associated with lower returns and profitability, consistent with negative cash flow effects. Within industries, higher biodiversity risk predicts higher returns. Our analysis of the geospatial measure reveals that firms with risky assets in biodiversity-sensitive areas earn higher returns. Thus, our results are consistent with a between-firm biodiversity risk premium. Our study contributes to a more nuanced understanding of biodiversity risk in asset pricing and offers new directions for climate and nature finance research.

title: The Fractality of Patronage: A Critical Realist Analysis of a Consciousness-Constrained Social System
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: The Fractality of Patronage: A Critical Realist Analysis of a Consciousness-Constrained Social System
detail.abstract: This conceptual paper advances a systems-theoretic framework to analyze the cross-scale recurrence of a specific social pattern: the stable structuration of relationships into hierarchical, triadic roles centered on asymmetrical resource dependency. This pattern, observed in systems ranging from families to nation-states, is characterized by the mutual reinforcement of patron, client, and instrumentalized roles. The analysis posits that this fractal persistence cannot be fully explained by scale-specific theories alone. Instead, drawing on a critical realist ontology, it is proposed that the pattern is generated by a deep-structural mechanism: the dominance of a collective "reactive-survival" operational consciousness. This mode privileges immediate psychological and structural homeostasis over long-term systemic optimization, thereby crystallizing social forms that reproduce dependency and limit agency. The paper further develops a model of social epigenetics to trace how this deep logic is imprinted in familial prototypes, rehearsed in secondary institutions, and crystallized at national scales, creating a self-sealing, morphostatic circuit. Synthesizing insights from family systems theory, political anthropology, and complex systems theory, this paradigmatic argument is presented as a heuristic model for reconceptualizing persistent social pathologies across micro, meso, and macro levels.

title: Computational Macrohistory Axiomatic Foundations for a Quantitative Science of Large-Scale Social Systems

detail.title: Computational Macrohistory Axiomatic Foundations for a Quantitative Science of Large-Scale Social Systems
detail.abstract: Computational Macrohistory (CMH) is proposed as a quantitative science that studies the temporal evolution of large-scale complex social systems through dynamic, probabilistic, and computational mathematical models. This document establishes the minimal, non-redundant set of axioms necessary for the discipline's foundation. Eight axioms (A1-A8) are formulated as admissibility constraints that any valid CMH model must satisfy, covering: statistical aggregation of collective behavior, conditioned historical ergodicity, structural causality, continuous temporal dynamics, endogenous indeterminacy, bounded reflexivity, predictive decay, and computational falsifiability. These axioms do not describe the world "as it is," but 1 CMH: Axiomatic Foundations rather define the conditions under which historical systems become scientifically tractable. Any model that violates one of these axioms falls outside the domain of Computational Macrohistory. This framework positions CMH as an extension and formalization of cliodynamics, providing rigorous mathematical foundations for predictive historical analysis while explicitly acknowledging epistemological limits. A minimal toy model is provided to demonstrate that the axiom set is jointly satisfiable.

title: Institutions and Growth in Mato Grosso: Land Market and Transports Shaping Divergent Paths between the North, Center-South, and Southwest

detail.title: Institutions and Growth in Mato Grosso: Land Market and Transports Shaping Divergent Paths between the North, Center-South, and Southwest

publicationDetails.detailsText: Espaço e Economia, volume 30, 2025[10.4000/15il9]

detail.abstract: This study analyzes the divergent agricultural growth trajectories across Mato Grosso's Mesoregions, demonstrating that the North's exceptional economic expansion cannot be explained by land increase alone but stems from two institutions: the Land Market and Transports. Using 2SLS regression and demographic analysis of Census data (1970-2006), the study shows that institutional changes implemented during Brazil's Military Regime (1964-1985) were fundamental drivers of this regional differentiation. The establishment of a formal land market through the 1964 Land Statute and the development of transport, particularly the BR-163 highway, reduced transaction and production costs in the North. These institutions enabled a 160.9% greater land incorporation compared to the Center-South baseline and attracted a working-age population (WAP) at double the rate of other regions. The analysis adapts Solow's neoclassical growth model to demonstrate how this institutional framework generated productivity gains through an increase in productive land per worker.

title: A Deterministic Framework for Adversarially Safe Liquidation Execution and Explicit Default Resolution in DeFi

detail.title: A Deterministic Framework for Adversarially Safe Liquidation Execution and Explicit Default Resolution in DeFi
detail.abstract: Aegis, a novel on-chain protocol designed to address the critical challenges of liquidation execution and default resolution in decentralized finance (DeFi). Existing systems often suffer from inefficiencies in liquidation processes and opaque loss allocation mechanisms, which can exacerbate systemic risks during market volatility. The proposed framework introduces a deterministic approach to liquidation rights delegation, enabling protocols to securely offload liquidation authority while maintaining transparency. Aegis incorporates a multi-format auction engine that supports Dutch auctions, sealed-bid auctions, and backstop execution, thereby optimizing collateral disposal under varying market conditions. Furthermore, the protocol implements a structured default resolution waterfall that explicitly defines the hierarchy of loss absorption, ranging from trader margins to residual debt tokenization, which mitigates ambiguity in deficit allocation. The system integrates robust oracle security mechanisms to ensure price validity through multi-source aggregation with bounded deviation checks. By combining these components into a unified LiquidationRouter, Aegis provides a composable and adversarially resilient solution for DeFi protocols. Our design advances the state of the art by formalizing liquidation execution as a deterministic process while explicitly codifying default resolution rules, thereby reducing uncertainty and improving systemic stability. The protocol's modular architecture allows for seamless integration with existing DeFi infrastructures, offering a practical yet theoretically grounded approach to managing credit risk in decentralized markets.

detail.abstract: Leadership is often highly visible and performative, yet the quieter work of stewardship is rarely acknowledged in Nigerian communities. This paper explores how young people in Lagos perceive different leadership styles-particularly those that prioritize public recognition and authority ("spotlight leadership") versus those that prioritize service, accountability, and responsibility ("stewardship"). Drawing on qualitative interviews, focus group discussions, and literature review, the study seeks to understand the values, expectations, and outcomes associated with these leadership approaches from the perspective of youth aged 18-30. It examines how perceptions of leadership influence civic engagement, trust in institutions, and participation in community initiatives. The study also considers how societal emphasis on visible leadership-awards, titles, and public recognition-shapes youth understanding of success, power, and responsibility. The findings are expected to contribute to broader discussions on leadership development, youth empowerment, and social development policy in Nigeria. By documenting the lived experiences, attitudes, and expectations of youth regarding leadership, the paper highlights the critical role of stewardship in shaping sustainable community and organizational outcomes. This preprint represents a working paper intended for early feedback, discussion, and iterative development prior to formal journal submission.

detail.title: Divergent Paths Of Agricultural Economic Growth In Immedi-Ate Regions Of Mato Grosso: The Impact Of Institutional
detail.abstract: This thesis examines the divergent paths of economic growth among the Immediate Regions of Mato Grosso, Brazil, stemming from institutional changes initiated during the Military Regime (1964-1985). This era catalyzed transformations with lasting consequences for the region's economic landscape, with some regions experiencing growth while others stagnated. The thesis tests the hypothesis that the nature of economic institutions, whether inclusive or extractive, played a decisive role in shaping these trajectories. Inclusive institutions, characterized by broad participation, secure property rights, and equitable access to resources, are considered promoters of economic dynamism. Extractive institutions, marked by concentrated power, insecure property rights, and limited access to opportunities, do not allow for sustained growth. The research employs a multifaceted approach, combining historical, econometric, and demographic analysis. The historical analysis traces the evolution of institutional structures in Mato Grosso. Econometric modeling, using data from the Agricultural and Demographic Censuses, evaluates the impact of Land Market development, Transports, and the emergence of Rural Enterprises on growth. Demographic analysis complements these components by examining population dynamics and labor force participation. The results reveal a pattern of regional differentiation where regions with more inclusive institutional changes experienced significant economic growth, driven by reduced transaction costs and increased productivity. Conversely, regions without these changes tended toward stagnation, as extractive institutions hindered economic diversification. These findings underscore the critical role of institutions in shaping long-term economic growth, where inclusive institutions are a catalyst for economic dynamism, while extractive institutions can trap regions in poverty and stagnation. This research suggests that targeted institutional reforms are crucial for unlocking the growth potential in similar contexts.

detail.abstract: Regulated financial and analytical platforms increasingly require browser-based user interfaces capable of visualising millions of data points in real time while remaining responsive, memory efficient, and auditable. Conventional rendering stacks based on SVG or the HTML Canvas API typically degrade beyond tens of thousands of primitives, leading to frame drops, excessive heap consumption, and unresponsive dashboards. Prior benchmarking indicates that SVG and Canvas performance begins to degrade around 10,000 graphical elements, while WebGL sustains higher throughput at substantially larger element counts by leveraging GPU parallelism and instanced rendering [1, 2]. In regulated environments, UI state itself can become part of the record that must be captured and preserved in a tamper-evident form under frameworks such as SEC Rule 17a-4 and FINRA Rule 4511 [3, 4]. This paper presents and evaluates a hybrid, multi-stage frontend architecture combining (i) WebGL for core geometry, (ii) a Canvas overlay for axes, labels, and interaction affordances, (iii) progressive streaming through GraphQL subscriptions, (iv) Web Worker + WebAssembly downsampling using the Largest-Triangle-Three-Buckets (LTTB) algorithm, and (v) React-based virtualization for bounded DOM complexity. Using controlled synthetic benchmarks up to 1.5 million points, the architecture sustains near-60 FPS interactions while maintaining heap memory below an 800 MB target and keeping time-tointeractive under two seconds. Beyond performance, the design integrates audit-aware observability by logging the rendered viewport, filters, and interaction context per render cycle to support reproducibility and retention requirements.

title: A Protocol-Only, Non-Custodial Settlement Layer for Composable DeFi Execution Efficiency

detail.title: A Protocol-Only, Non-Custodial Settlement Layer for Composable DeFi Execution Efficiency
detail.abstract: Netting-by-Constraint (NBC), a protocol-only, non-custodial settlement layer that optimizes execution efficiency in composable decentralized finance (DeFi) through deterministic claim netting. The current on-chain settlement landscape suffers from redundant transfers and fragmented liquidity, which inflates gas costs and latency; NBC addresses this by introducing a constraint-based netting mechanism that aggregates compatible payment obligations without intermediate custody. The protocol operates on a tuple-based claim model, where each claim specifies asset, amount bounds, destination, and directional flow, then enforces netting compatibility through strict overlap conditions across three distinct claim classes with varying settlement properties. A deterministic grouping algorithm processes these claims, canceling opposing flows within intersecting ranges while preserving conservation of value and noncustodial execution invariants. Furthermore, the economic model incorporates execution fees and irreversibility premiums to align incentives with protocol security. The design achieves backward compatibility with existing DeFi systems by exposing a claim submission interface that requires no modifications to downstream logic. Experimental results demonstrate significant reductions in on-chain footprint, with Class A claims exhibiting near-instant finality and Class B/C providing configurable trade-offs between netting efficiency and settlement urgency. This work advances the state of composable execution layers by formalizing a minimalistic, protocolnative approach to payment netting that maintains decentralization guarantees while eliminating redundant on-chain operations.

title: BITNEKO: Bridging Ancestral Wisdom with Digital Innovation

detail.title: BITNEKO: Bridging Ancestral Wisdom with Digital Innovation
detail.abstract:
What if Satoshi were a Salvadoran artisan? BITNEKO as proof that true consensus does not reside in code, but in collective perception.

BITNEKO is presented as a decentralized cultural symbol emerging at the intersection of Bitcoin, ancestral tradition, and perceptual theory. Originating in El Salvador during the historic adoption of Bitcoin as legal tender, BITNEKO operates not as a financial asset, token, or investment instrument, but as an open cultural protocol and a public-domain archetype.

This paper situates BITNEKO within the broader framework of the Panperceptual Theory of the Universe (TPU), introducing Proof of Perception (PoP) as a proposed paradigm for decentralized validation based on resonance, symbolic depth, and perceptual complexity, rather than computational power or capital accumulation.

Through cultural analysis, theoretical modeling, philosophical critique, and formal constructs such as the Perceptual Wave Function (PWF) and the Perceptual Complexity Index (IPC), the document argues for a shift from mechanistic consensus models toward perceptual architectures capable of integrating human, artificial, and non-human observers. BITNEKO is examined as a living cultural experiment that empirically illustrates how consensus emerges through resonance rather than authority.

At the critical threshold where artificial intelligence begins to co-create reality, humanity faces an existential paradox: our most advanced technologies operate on 17th-century Cartesian foundations, while our understanding of consciousness and reality has evolved radically. This work not only identifies this epistemological gap but proposes a complete ontological framework for the next era of conscious digital systems.

title: Exchange Rate Based Inflation Stabilization Plans and Exports Composition
affiliations: Universidad Torcuato di Tella

detail.title: Exchange Rate Based Inflation Stabilization Plans and Exports Composition
detail.abstract: Inflation stabilization plans have often relied on exchange rate pegs to reduce inflation. I document a new empirical finding: following the implementation of such plans, sectors that use capital more intensively in production increase their share in total exports. Using COMTRADE data and a proxy for capital-intensive sectors, I show that this pattern holds across countries that implemented exchange rate–based stabilization plans. I also document the same pattern for Argentina’s 1991 stabilization plan, where direct measures of sectoral production functions are available. To analyze the mechanism behind this result, I develop a multisector general equilibrium model with heterogeneous production functions in the exportable sector. The model is calibrated to Argentina’s 1991 plan, one of the longest and most studied inflation stabilization plans, and replicates both the observed change in export composition and the main stylized facts highlighted in the literature. The key mechanism driving the reallocation in exports is the change in relative prices between capital and labor induced by the stabilization plan.

detail.abstract: This study examines the relationship between the perceived threat of immigrants and the support for punitive immigration policies and the exclusion of immigrants, achieved by merging immigration and criminal law (crimmigration). Based on the literature of Stumpf (2006), the membership theory and the group threat theory, the expected result is that the perceived threat of immigrants is positively related to the support for punitive immigration policies and the exclusion of immigrants. This argumentation rests on the findings that the perceived threat is positively related to the willingness to expel people from the ingroup and to the support for punitive policies. Based on the data gathered through a survey conducted on the online crowdsourcing platform MTurk, the findings of this study confirm the hypotheses. People who perceive immigrants as a higher threat tend to show more support for punitive immigration policies and their exclusion from society. These findings give an indication of the influence of prejudice in policy development and how it can lead to crimmigration and laws disproportionally targeting certain groups. This study contributes to the existing literature in two ways, first, it divides crimmigration into two separate but intertwined aspects which enable connections to existing literature. Second, it provides a unique and comprehensive insight into the drivers of crimmigration supported by empirical quantitative research.

title: DenariumX: A Time-Disciplined Framework for Monetary Issuance and Credibility

detail.title: DenariumX: A Time-Disciplined Framework for Monetary Issuance and Credibility
detail.abstract: Contemporary monetary systems exhibit a fundamental flaw that transcends mere excessive issuance: the lack of enforceable temporal discipline. Monetary value is generally perceived as a quantity independent of time, which permits delayed actions, policy lag, and discretionary interventions to distort economic signals without incurring formal penalties. Consequently, money frequently mirrors past conditions instead of reflecting the current synchronized economic reality. This paper presents DenariumX, an innovative monetary framework that regards time as a primary economic constraint. Rather than depending on scarcity narratives, market incentives, or discretionary policy modifications, DenariumX mandates issuance validity through protocollevel time windows. Monetary units are deemed valid solely when generated within specified temporal limits; any deviations are automatically rendered invalid or eliminated through rulebased penalty mechanisms. DenariumX is purposefully non-speculative and does not presuppose circulation, exchange, or price discovery. It is proposed as a research and simulation framework aimed at assessing whether time-consistent issuance can bolster monetary credibility, mitigate inflationary drift resulting from delayed responses, and reconceptualize money as a measure of synchronized economic activity rather than merely a repository of speculative value. This paper provides a conceptual foundation for empirical testing of time-disciplined monetary design in controlled settings.

title: Damped Market Design: A Certified Efficiency-Volatility-Influence Frontier
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Damped Market Design: A Certified Efficiency-Volatility-Influence Frontier
detail.abstract: Repeated markets publish price statistics; deviations can change the distribution of the released tape. We study a dual-channel architecture: an internal statistic p t determines allocations and payments, while the public tape releases pt = Bin ∆ (p t + ξ t). Measuring tape influence by total variation, we derive a distribution-free certificate: if a coalition can shift p t by at most δk , then tape influence is bounded by the corresponding noise shift, and postprocessing cannot increase influence. For Laplace noise this bound inverts in closed form, mapping an influence cap to a required injected noise variance (quadratic in k under linear envelopes). Coupled with an accuracy requirement on the tape, the certificate yields a feasibility diagnostic. Combining with equilibrium-implied sensitivity and internal variance gives a computable efficiency-variance-influence constraint. We provide the equilibrium objects for the Damped Auction (runner-up wins and pays her bid), which exhibits upper-tail pooling for n ≥ 5.

detail.abstract: This paper reports a comprehensive interdisciplinary project to develop an analytical rubric for online and blended learning framed by the model of Teaching Presence. The project's purpose was to create a robust 'theory-based' instrument to complement the use of Student Evaluation of Teaching (SET) surveys, a method that dominates the assessment of course and teaching quality in Higher Education. Extending over multiple stages of development and testing, the final rubric comprises 23 teaching activities covering the three Teaching Presence functions: 1. Design and Organisation, 2. Facilitating Discourse, and 3. Direct Instruction. As part of the final testing stage, 36 Teaching Presence rubrics were administered by the project team to 12 courses across a range of undergraduate programs and levels of learning. Support for the rubric's design is provided by strong inter-rater reliability, calculated using Gwet's Agreement Coefficient 2 (Gwet's AC2). The Teaching Presence rubric is demonstrated to be a reliable instrument that can effectively contribute to the evaluation of course and teaching quality in online and blended HE programs.
