detail.abstract: Interest in labor unions has resurged in the United States, yet many workers remain ambivalent about whether unions help or hurt them. At the same time, managerial opposition to unions is widespread, but firms differ sharply in whether they make that opposition public. In an interactive wage-bargaining experiment, we find that publicly disclosing managerial opposition to unions increases effort and realized wages for workers with an anti-union stance, but does not generate similar gains for workers with a pro-union stance. This divergence arises because the same disclosure triggers heterogeneous belief updating. For anti-union workers, who initially doubt the benefits of collective bargaining, disclosed managerial opposition to unions provides new information about relative bargaining power. Specifically, they learn through the disclosure that managers prefer individual bargaining because it allows them to use wage-setting discretion to tie pay closely to individual performance, while collective bargaining may strengthen workers' bargaining position more than previously believed. Pro-union workers, in contrast, learn little new from the disclosure. Instead, it confirms their prior beliefs, leaving effort incentives unchanged. Overall, our study provides causal evidence that the disclosure of managerial opposition to unions itself, apart from any accompanying tactics, can materially shape worker productivity and pay.

title: Optimal Bayesian Online Allocation of Reusable Resources
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business,  and University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: Optimal Bayesian Online Allocation of Reusable Resources
detail.abstract:
Many modern online platforms allocate "reusable" capacity, where a resource unit is occupied for some duration and then becomes available again. Examples include cloud and edge computing platforms allocating compute or GPU memory to jobs, rental marketplaces, and service systems in which capacity cycles between busy and idle states. Motivated by these applications, we study a Bayesian online resource allocation problem with reusable resources.  There are k units of each resource, and demand requests of heterogeneous types (i.e., rewards and usage durations) arrive according to non-stationary Poisson processes. Upon arrival, each request must be irrevocably assigned at most one unit of a resource. The goal is to maximize the total expected reward. Our main result is a simple online algorithm that obtains a 1-\sqrt{2/\pi k} + O(1/k) fraction of the reward obtained by the optimal omniscient algorithm. Our results advance the existing literature by directly generalizing the non-reusable setting of  Wang et al. (2018) to the reusable setting, matching the best known bound in the non-reusable case, and hence solving an open problem by improving upon the best previously known guarantee of 1-O(\sqrt{\log k/k}) for reusable resources due to Feng, Niazadeh, and Saberi (2024).

Our results are obtained through a now-standard propose--then--admit framework. We upper bound the performance of the optimal omniscient algorithm by a fluid LP approximation, and then round the optimal fluid solution. Each request first proposes to a resource type according to the LP assignment probabilities, and then each resource runs an online admission-control policy to enforce ex-post capacity feasibility. Our main contribution is a simple and novel state-dependent admission-control policy for reusable resources that yields a constant per-proposal admission probability of Pr[Poisson(k)<= k-1 | Poisson(k) <= k] independent of time, rewards, or durations, which immediately leads to our main result. Our policy equalizes conditional admission probabilities (conditional on a request being made) among all potential requests. To this end, it synthetically increases the load at each time (so that the total load is exactly equal to the capacity) by adding "imaginary" requests when necessary, and then greedily accepting real and imaginary requests.

title: Dynamics of Conserved Settlement
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Dynamics of Conserved Settlement
detail.abstract: This paper develops a dynamic model of external adjustment in an N-country system operating under conserved settlement of a neutral reserve asset. Neutral reserve holdings evolve according to a conservation law, while exchange rates adjust through uncovered interest parity and trade-balance responses. The resulting system links reserve holdings, interest differentials, and exchange-rate movements through a coupled dynamic structure. The model shows that when settlement assets are conserved rather than elastically expandable, external imbalances generate endogenous adjustment dynamics. Reserve imbalances induce exchange-rate changes that restore trade balance. Adjustment oscillates around equilibrium until damping gradually restores balance over time. The analysis demonstrates how conserved settlement transforms external balance into an emergent property of the system, consistent with Conserved Settlement Theory (CST). Balanced external accounts arise as the unique steady state implied by conservation constraints.

title: Elastic Capacity, Leverage, and Settlement Constraints
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Elastic Capacity, Leverage, and Settlement Constraints
detail.abstract: Financial systems defer settlement through balance-sheet expansion, allowing liabilities to grow alongside assets while preserving the accounting identity A = L + E. This paper shows that such elasticity is structurally limited by leverage constraints implied by this identity. Because losses reduce equity one-for-one while liability expansion raises leverage mechanically, admissible balance-sheet growth converges toward zero as leverage approaches its maximum level. When this constraint binds, outstanding net claims can no longer be absorbed through liability issuance. The system therefore shifts from liability expansion to valuation adjustment. A conserved settlement quantity whose stock is independent of liability creation becomes the remaining mechanism through which accounts may close, yielding a valuation rule linking residual claims directly to price. The analysis establishes elastic capacity exhaustion as an accounting property and provides a foundation for subsequent analysis of emergence dynamics in conserved settlement systems.

title: The Triffin Constraint under Conserved Settlement
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The Triffin Constraint under Conserved Settlement
detail.abstract: The Triffin dilemma describes the structural tension faced by reserve-currency systems in which global liquidity provision is tied to persistent external deficits of the issuing country. This paper shows that the dilemma arises from the accounting structure of liability-based reserve settlement rather than from specific institutional arrangements. When international settlement occurs through a conserved, non-sovereign reserve asset whose price floats relative to sovereign currencies, the requirement that any single country supply reserves through sustained deficits no longer applies. External adjustment instead proceeds through redistribution of a conserved settlement stock, with marginal adjustment occurring through price and exchange-rate responses rather than expansion of reserve liabilities. The analysis constitutes one component of a broader framework describing international adjustment under conserved settlement within the Neutral Reserve Settlement Model (NRSM).

title: The Effects of Starlink adoption on forest degradation in the Amazon

detail.title: The Effects of Starlink adoption on forest degradation in the Amazon

detail.abstract: Satellite broadband is rapidly expanding into remote regions, promising social and economic gains but also reshaping the landscape for illicit activity. In the Brazilian Amazon, Starlink’s entry in 2022 improved internet access in municipalities with limited mobile coverage. Using Starlink data from 772 Amazonian municipalities between 2022 and 2024, we found that increased connectivity led to greater forest degradation, mainly caused by wildfires, and the conversion of forests to non-forest areas and pastures, consistent with the use of fire as a low-cost land-clearing method. The expansion of Starlink was also associated with increased levels of particulate matter, including smaller size fractions (PM2.5 and PM1). We found no evidence of a strengthened enforcement response to overall or fire-related infractions, suggesting that connectivity benefits were primarily exploited by environmental offenders. These findings reveal the unexpected environmental and social costs of satellite internet expansion in the Amazon, highlighting the need for improved enforcement as connectivity grows.

title: Conserved Settlement Theory
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Conserved Settlement Theory
detail.abstract: Classical trade theory predicts efficient specialization through comparative advantage under conditions of balanced exchange, while modern international macroeconomics observes persistent external imbalances sustained by financial intermediation. This paper argues that the apparent tension arises from an implicit assumption regarding the nature of international settlement. We introduce Conserved Settlement Theory (CST), which embeds settlement constraints directly into a Ricardian production environment using an accounting identity linking current account balances to financial liabilities and settlement transfers. Distinguishing between elastic and conserved settlement regimes, we show that when settlement becomes conserved, persistent external imbalance becomes infeasible and the competitive equilibrium coincides with the Ricardian allocation. The resulting allocation constitutes a Nash equilibrium of decentralized international trade, as no country can sustain welfare-improving deviations through persistent external imbalance. Comparative advantage is therefore preserved while balanced exchange emerges endogenously as a feasibility condition rather than an assumption. The analysis implies that macroeconomic instability arises not from failures of trade efficiency but from elastic settlement mechanisms that permit imbalances to accumulate through expanding financial claims. Conserved settlement restores trade clearance through price adjustment while maintaining efficient specialization.

title: Bayesian Two-Sample Survival Probability Curves with Comparative Summary Measures and Sensitivity Analyses

detail.title: Bayesian Two-Sample Survival Probability Curves with Comparative Summary Measures and Sensitivity Analyses
detail.abstract: Two-sample survival probability curves (TSSPC) provide a concise way to visualize treatment survival distribution differences in randomized controlled trials. We propose various area under the curve (AUC) measures for TSSPCs as treatment effect numerical measures. The proposed restricted AUC (R-AUC) can be estimated regardless of the survival curve estimate completeness due to censoring and has a clear probabilistic interpretation. Additionally, we introduce sensitivity analysis measures, the worst- and best-case AUC (W-AUC and B-AUC), to represent treatment effect extreme cases beyond a restriction time point. We further propose to estimate the TSSPC and AUC measures using two Bayesian models and compare them with their Kaplan-Meier (KM) and Cox proportional hazards (PH) model-based counterparts in four oncology clinical trials. We find that when the PH assumption holds, all methods give similar estimates, whereas when it is violated, the proposed Bayesian estimators outperform the Cox model. In all studied scenarios, the more flexible person-period Bayesian approach provides similar flexibility, but smoother curve estimation compared to the KM approach. In the presence of moderate to heavy administrative censoring, we recommend using R-AUC, together with the W- and B-AUCs, as supportive treatment effect measures for the TSSPC regardless of the chosen estimator.

title: Labour Productivity Indicators at the Country and Industry Level: Induced Misinterpretation, With Political Consequences
affiliations: Autonomous University of Barcelona

detail.title: Labour Productivity Indicators at the Country and Industry Level: Induced Misinterpretation, With Political Consequences
detail.abstract: Periodic data on labour productivity at country and industry level has become a familiar topic not only in academia but in the media and the socio-political debate on Labour policies and economic growth. However, It should be noted in this regard that the data regularly released by public statistics agencies does not actually tell us about the productivity of the Labour force in the sense usually understood by general public and that is conveyed more professionally by the media as well as experts to their audiences; namely, that an increase indicates that in the country (or industry) companies are producing more quantities of products or services on average with the same staff (and equipment, facilities, etc.), or producing the same with fewer resources, and so on. This paper aims to demonstrate why the standard labour productivity ratios and indexes regularly released by public agencies do not in fact have the commonly assumed meaning; which inevitably mystifies the social discourse on wage policy, workers' bargaining, and labour policies.

title: Neutral Reserve Settlement Model: A Multi-Country Framework for External Adjustment
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Neutral Reserve Settlement Model: A Multi-Country Framework for External Adjustment
detail.abstract: This paper develops the Neutral Reserve Settlement Model (NRSM), a multi-country framework in which external imbalances are settled through a conserved, non-sovereign reserve asset whose price floats relative to sovereign currencies. Exchange rates and reserve prices jointly transmit settlement imbalances, allowing external adjustment to occur without bilateral targeting rules or persistent liability expansion. The model formalizes accounting constraints, price adjustment, and exchange-rate dynamics in a unified structure and shows that conserved settlement preserves Ricardian comparative advantage while endogenously compressing external imbalances. The framework provides the discrete-time implementation underlying the continuous-time dynamics developed in companion work within Conserved Settlement Theory (CST).

title: The Emergence of Conserved Settlement
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The Emergence of Conserved Settlement
detail.abstract: This paper develops a model of settlement in which outstanding financial claims are resolved through leveraged balance-sheet expansion, official absorption, or the use of a conserved neutral reserve asset. Elastic settlement is bounded by aggregate leverage capacity proportional to financial system equity. When settlement demand approaches elastic capacity, equilibrium requires residual adjustment through the neutral reserve asset. The model reduces settlement dynamics to a single state variable-leverage slack-which governs system behavior. As slack declines, settlement transitions continuously from liability-based to asset based adjustment. The framework predicts gradual emergence of neutral reserve settlement, rising price sensitivity near constraint boundaries, and increasing informational content of the neutral reserve price prior to systemic stress. The neutral reserve price corresponds to the shadow value of scarce settlement capacity.

detail.abstract: Institutional anxiety is proposed as a measurable systemic variable that predicts the likelihood of non-decision in complex organizational and governance contexts. Unlike performance metrics or crisis indicators, institutional anxiety reflects internal perceptions of risk, responsibility, and exposure that influence decision behavior prior to observable failure. This paper develops a conceptual and analytical framework for identifying, quantifying, and interpreting institutional anxiety across public administration, education, and healthcare systems. The study demonstrates how institutional anxiety shapes procedural behavior, delays strategic action, and constrains adaptive capacity. By operationalizing institutional anxiety as a predictive factor, policymakers and organizational designers can identify latent vulnerabilities, calibrate decision responsibilities, and preserve adaptive functionality under uncertainty.
